 JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 06.10.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 06.10.2021 at about 6.45am the petitioner was returning to his home in his Two wheeler Bajaj Discover bearing Reg.No.KA01EX8993 on BB Road, Opposite to Jakkur Aerodrome, Yelahanka, after completion of his night shift duty at Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka, there was drizzling and mist.

While he was so riding on the said road under the bridge on his vehicle, a Tata Gas Tanker bearing Reg.NO.KA01AG 8476 suddenly stopped on the said road without giving any indication, as a result of which, his bike dashed to the back side of the said Gas Tanker.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down towards right side and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Rail Wheel Factory Hospital, Yelahanka.

After first aid he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient, underwent surgeries and after necessary treatment discharged on 18.10.2021 with an advice for follow up treatment.

Thereafter again on 18.10.2021 he was admitted to Hosmat Hospital for further management due to grievous head injury, wherein he was treated conservatively till 20.10.2021 and discharged with advice to take physiotherapy.
After one week of discharge petitioner became abnormal due to head injuries.

On account of petitioner's behavior he was admitted again to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, diagnosed as 'delirium secondary to his medical condition' and later discharged on 03.11.2021 with advice to take follow up treatment with complete bed rest for 3 months.
The petitioner was again admitted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, treated from 27.12.2021 to 30.12.2021.

So far he has spent Rs.15,00,000/ towards treatment, conveyance,
attendance, nourishment, food and other incidental charges.

4. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy,
working as a Senior Technician in RailWheel Factory at Yelahanka and getting salary of Rs.75,000/ per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he has not attended the duty till 14.03.2022.
On account of this disability he has to take maximum rest at home.
Hence, the petitioner and his family members are undergoing great mental shock and agony and financial loss.

The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA 01AG8476 and the Yelahanka Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata Gas Tanker in Cr.No.170/2021 p/u/Sec.279, 283 & 338 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the incharge owner and the 3 rd respondent being the insurer of the Tata Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA 01AG8476 are jointly and severally liable to Raghunath.N vs Praxair India Pvt Ltd on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26229909/
2 pay compensation to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence, this petition.
5. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statements.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 did not appear before this court hence, placed exparte.
6. The objections of the Respondent No.3:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA 01 AG8476.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) & Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the accident.
The driver of the Gas Tanker did not have an effective and valid DL and vehicle was plying without valid permit.

The Respondent insurer has further denied the manner of accident, petitioner's age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioner and has sought for dismissal of the petition.
7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 06.10.2021 at 6.45am due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of TATA Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA01AG 8476 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom payable?
3. What order or award?
8. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 17 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.17.
He has also examined Smt. Shanthamma S. - MRO as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.18 to P.23.

And Sri Shankar - MRO at M.S. Ramaiah Hospita, Mathikere,
Bangalore got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.24 to P.28.
Dr.Krishna Prasad got examined as PW.4 and got marked Exs.P.29 & 30.
On the other side, the Respondent No.3 has got examined Mr.Naveena S.  Legal Manager as RW.1 and did not mark any document.
9. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
ACJ 2022 Kar Page 377: Srinivasa G. Shetty Vs. A.N.Manjunath and Ors.
10.

sentences.text: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA01AG8476 the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination, he has admitted that the accident occurred on October 2021.
On the date of accident he was going alone to his house from factory.
The bike belongs to him and it has insurance.

He has also examined MRO of Hosmat Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.18 to 23,
authorization letter, outpatient records, inpatient records, copy of police intimation,
MLC register extract and Xrays 7 in Nos.

During the cross examination of PW.2,
nothing worthwhile is elicited.
He has also examined MRO of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.24 to P.28, authorization letter, inpatient file, Xray CT, Police intimation and MLC Extract.

There was no cross examination by the Respondent No.3.
12.
The FIR was registered on the same day of accident i.e., on 06.10.2021 on the complaint of petitioner's son at Ex.P.1.
Ex . P.2
is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the Gas Tanker after thorough investigation.
Ex . P.3
spot mahazar was done on 06.10.2021 and accident spot was investigated.
Ex.P.4 is the sketch shows the accident spot.
Ex. P.5
MVA report shows that Tata 2518c multi axle oxygen tanker no visible damages found and Bajaj Discover 125 damages and Head light assembly damaged.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of notice and reply u/Sec.133 of MV Act and Ex.P.8 is the copy of ordersheet in CC No.10475/2021.
These documents support the case of the petitioner.
The respondent No.3 did not produce any document nor examined any witness in support of their contention to prove the negligence of the petitioner.
Therefore the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the TATA Gas Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA01AG8476.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has examined Dr.Krishna Prasad as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.29 & 30 Xrays 2 in Nos. with reports and OPD file.

He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and has stated about the physical disability of combining 1 & 2 upper limb spine and lower limb disability is 58% and to the whole body at 20%.
14. During the cross examination of PW.3, he has stated that the petitioner is central Government Employee in Railways.
Government Employee rejoins duty on submission of FC.
Upper limb fractures are united, but the implants at right wrist are in situ.
The petitioner has problem with the range of movements of the wrist even though the fractures are united and the muscle power is normal.
15. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident he was working as a Senior Technician at Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka and getting salary of Rs.75,000/ per month.

From the evidence of PW.4 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact his work and Raghunath.N vs Praxair India Pvt Ltd on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26229909/
4 throughout his life.

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed the income of the deceased on the basis of economic conditions prevailing in foreign countries as the deceased was working in Abudhabi.
In the case on hand, the Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Senior Technician at Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka and getting salary of Rs.75,000/ per month.
However, he has not examined his employer.
In the cross examination of PW.1, he has admitted that he is still working in Rail Wheel Factory.
As of November 2023 his Gross salary is around Rs.1,03,000/.
As per salary slip of October 2021 he has received the salary for the whole month and also received salary from November 2021 to April 2022.
Therefore, as per his admissions and based on Ex.P.17

the Tribunal deems it fit to fix the gross income of the petitioner at Rs.90,000/
per month.
17. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 56 years as could be made out from Ex.P.10/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2021.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital and Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore as an inpatient from 06.10.2021 to 18.10.2021, 18.10.2021 to 20.10.2021 and 27.10.2021 to 03.11.2021 and discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summaries.
Considering that the nature of injuries he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent Rs.15,00,000/ towards hospitalization, medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills 40 in Nos. as per Ex.P.12 for a sum of Rs.29,682/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent No.3.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
During his cross examination he has stated that from the month of November 2021 to April 2022 he has not received incentives since he did not attend the work.

In this regard he has not produced any documents like Leave transactions, letter from the employer Raghunath.N vs Praxair India Pvt Ltd on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26229909/
5 pertaining to the leave information or EL details.

sentences.text: The petitioner has taken treatment for 22 days at M.S.Ramaiah Hospital and at Hosmat hospital which can be made out from Ex.P.11 Discharge summaris.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,80,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
Due to the disability the petitioner was neither demoted nor has he lost any income or his capacity of earning.
Therefore, he is not entitled to any amount under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 56 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 20% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 22 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.75,000/
under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the version of PW.4, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants of right wrist which will costs around Rs.65,000/ and he needs right ankle fusion in future when the pain becomes intense which will cost Rs.1.2 Lakhs.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.4 have not produced any estimation bills.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.40,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/ under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.1,00,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.29,682/

Loss of income during laid up period Rs.1,80,000/
4. Loss of future income - NIL  5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.50,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.75,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs.40,000/ TOTAL Rs.4,74,682/ If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.4,75,000/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 19.
The Respondent No.3 has contended that the accident occurred on the sole negligence of the petitioner himself.

In order to prove the same, it has got examined their Legal Manager as RW.1,
who filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination reiterating the objections.
But he did not mark any documents on his behalf.
During the cross examination of RW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
Therefore, the Respondents being the Owners and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.3/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.4,75,000 with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,75,000/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Seventy Five Thousand only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.3/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
